=======================================================
 BHARAT MOHANDAS BHARWANI  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT =======================================================
Appearance:
MR SURAJ A SHUKLA(7185) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 HCLS COMMITTEE(4998) for the Respondent(s) No. 1 MR KIRTAN H MISTRY(10012) for the Respondent(s) No. 1 MR RAJENDRA D JADHAV(10026) for the Respondent(s) No. 1 MR DHAWAN JAYSWAL APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 =======================================================

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of notice of rule for respondent - State of Gujarat.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.11210054232918/2023 registered with the Sachin Police Station, Surat for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 465, 467 and 468 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Learned advocate, Mr. Suraj Shukla for the applicant submitted that the so-called incident has taken place on 22.10.2023, for which, the FIR has been lodged on 04.11.2023 and the applicant has been arrested in connection with the same on NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22153/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined 05.11.2023 and since then, he is in judicial custody.

sentences.text:
Learned advocate submitted that as per the case of the prosecution, the present applicant has received amount from the complainant and given assurance that he will give shop in the complex,
which was constructed by him, however, some disputes have been cropped up between the applicant and the complainant, therefore, FIR has been registered against the present applicant, however now the issue has been resolved between the parties and the complainant has also filed an undertaking to the effect that he has no objection if the present application can be entertained.
Learned advocate further submitted that at the time of registration of the FIR, the complainant has stated about another incident, wherein the applicant is involved.

Learned advocate, however, submitted that the applicant is a builder and he has constructed one complex and at the time of constructing the building, certain work had been carried out by the said person and in lieu of the work, the present applicant has to pay certain amount to other persons and, hence, an agreement to sale came to be executed between them to sale out the shop situated in the said complex.

Learned advocate submitted that however thereafter, the said agreement to sale was cancelled and another agreement to sale was executed between the parties and subsequently, the said agreement was also cancelled and they have entered into Memorandum of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22153/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined Understanding and as per the said MOU, the present applicant has to handover the cheques of equal amount for the work carried out by the said victim and as per the said MOU, the applicant has already handed over the cheque to the victim, therefore as such, the said victim has not got any valuable right to raise objection in the present matter against the applicant as the matter has been settled between the applicant and the complainant.

It is, therefore,
urged that considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
4. Learned APP for the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
It is submitted that the role of the present applicant is clearly spelt out from the papers of the chargesheet and, hence, the present application may not be entertained.

5. Learned advocate, Mr. Kirtan Mistry appearing for the original complainant has confirmed about the settlement arrived at between the applicant and the complainant and also stated that the complainant has also filed an affidavit to the effect that he has no objection if the present application is allowed and the applicant may be granted bail.

6. Learned advocate, Mr. Rajendra Jadav appearing for the victim viz., Ismail Ibrahim Dodiya has opposed the grant of present application and submitted NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22153/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined that the present applicant is habitual offender and number of persons have been duped by him and there are total 10 cases under the provision of the Negotiable Instrument Act registered against the applicant and those cases are pending before the competent criminal court for adjudication.

Learned advocate further submitted that it is true that on two occasions, the present applicant - accused has given assurance to the victim by entering into an agreement to sale but then after subsequently, he has been backed off from his earlier assurances by cancelling the said documents.

Learned advocate submitted that in fact, the present applicant has also executed MOU in favour of the victim specifically stating that by handing over cheque, assurance has been given by the applicant that as and when the cheque would be deposited, it would be honoured and the dispute between them would be settled but in fact,

2 whenever the victim had tried to deposit the cheque, the applicant - accused made excuses under one pretext or other and did not permit the victim to deposit the cheque and thereby killed the valuable time but this is a systematic modus operandi adopted by the present applicant - accused.

sentences.text: Learned advocate submitted that yet the investigation is going on and the present application is filed at pre-mature stage before submission of the chargesheet and, hence, same may not be considered.

Learned advocate submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22153/2023 ORDER DATED:
16/01/2024 undefined the victim has come to know from some reliable sources that number of persons (victims) have been duped by the applicant - accused, which clearly goes on to show that the present applicant is habitual offender.
It is, therefore, urged that considering the above factual aspects, the present application may not be entertained.

7. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.
8. It is found out from the record that the present application is preferred after submission of the chargesheet and now the investigation is completed and the applicant is in jail since 05.11.2023.
I have considered the role played by the applicant at the time of commission of crime.
Further as stated above, the matter is settled out of the Court and the complainant, by filing an affidavit, has given consent for the grant of regular bail.
Further in the present FIR, the complainant has no right to raise any objection, for which, separate proceeding can be initiated.
Almost investigation is over.
Therefore considering the above factual aspects and also on the ground of settlement arrived at between the applicant and the complainant, the present application deserves to be allowed.

9. This Court has also taken into consideration the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22153/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40 as well as in case of Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51.
10.

11. Hence, the present application is allowed.

sentences.text: The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the concerned Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
13. At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court while enlarging the applicant on bail.
14. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
